# Evgenii Zaitsev

## Pages
- [Evgenii Zaitsev - Product Manager](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/): Evgenii Zaitsev, Product Manager and EmTalk founder. B2B and B2C, complex products, analytics and teams. Samolet, EmTalk and consulting case studies, CV and contact details.
- [AI products and tools](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/ai/): Decision Matrix, hybrid RAG, articles, courses, video and analytics. How our tools work and where people remain part of the process.
- [Cases](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/): Product problems, decisions and the stages we reached. Explore by experience and topic.
- [Checking more than code: Codex, OpenCode and output quality](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/ai-agent-orchestration/): We had written a PDF verifier, but the main build never ran it. A second agent found the gap. This is how I separate implementation from verification, and why one convincing model response is not enough.
- [Working with AI: context, specifications and a verifiable result](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/ai-sdd-workflow/): How I organise agent-assisted work on this site: facts and requirements stay in the project, while readiness is checked separately from how convincing an answer sounds.
- [EmTalk: from sources to an article and a narration script](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-articles/): A volunteer team cannot make article production sustainable simply by asking AI to write faster. For wellbeing content, the more important task is a controlled path from suitable sources to a draft a person can review.
- [Scripts and music: creative choices within verifiable constraints](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-audio/): An appealing model response is not enough to assemble an audio experience. In EmTalk's pipeline, a script passes through a judge and editor, while its music plan is checked for timing, transitions and alignment with speech.
- [EmTalk: a course is built in stages, not with one AI prompt](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-courses/): A long piece of text does not automatically become a course. EmTalk's educational workflow separates structure, lesson planning, materials and knowledge checks into distinct stages.
- [Not one model for everything: routine work, generation and review](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-model-routing/): Extracting a field, proposing a structure and checking an article require different work. At EmTalk, I separate those operations: code handles formal rules, lower-cost models take on some routine work, and output quality is checked separately.
- [EmTalk: build the knowledge base before asking AI to write](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-rag/): A well-written answer does not necessarily rest on suitable sources. In EmTalk's AI workflow, preparing knowledge is a separate process: find material, preserve its provenance and assemble context for the task.
- [One story across platforms, with publishing kept separate](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-social/): A carousel, a short post and a LinkedIn article need different treatments. EmTalk has an active workflow definition for carousel preparation and a separate prototype exploring ideas and platform adaptation.
- [Video for EmTalk: when views met production cost](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-video-economics/): Two short videos received around two thousand views each. When we tried to make longer videos more often, the important number became the cost of a usable video, not the price of one generation.
- [From carousel to video, with room for human intervention](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ai-video/): The model proposes scenes, but does not decide on its own what reaches the final video. EmTalk's pipeline checks the plan in code and allows an individual scene to be replaced manually.
- [Why we put venture funding on hold and focused on learning](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-community/): While developing our first prototypes, we considered venture funding. The proposed terms made us assess the pace and working model we were ready to sustain.
- [The EmTalk team: what helps people keep working together](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-culture/): Some EmTalk contributors have stayed with the project for two years or longer. I looked for a way of working that connects product development with people's own goals.
- [EmTalk discovery: from audience segments to MVP options](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-discovery/): How do you turn a broad idea about well-being into a product problem? Our research workbook brought together audiences, alternative models, questions and options for the first scope of work.
- [Decision Matrix: AI suggests options, people make the decision](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-dm-product/): Choosing a project, a career move or one of several ideas can be difficult. At EmTalk, we are developing a product that helps people see their options, compare them and understand the reasoning behind a choice.
- [From one super app to four EmTalk directions](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-ecosystem/): Contributors were growing tired while the large app still needed substantial work. We reconsidered the super-app format and split its value into several connected product directions.
- [Try before installing: bringing EmTalk's first value to the browser](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-first-value/): Clicking Download does not mean someone has received value. I chose to let visitors try the core BRET or Decision Matrix flow directly on the website first.
- [TAPL: from a task list to learning around the user's routine](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-tapl/): TAPL started as a to-do idea. We reconsidered its value, developed an EdTech concept and explored it with external users. The product has gone through pivots and continues to develop gradually.
- [The first team broke apart: continuing EmTalk](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-team/): We started with a B2C product idea and a team that wanted to keep working after the incubator. Our first major turning point came in the relationships between team members.
- [Why EmTalk moved from Webflow to Hugo](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-web-migration/): We were already working on the site through MCP and AI agents. I reconsidered the platform itself: paying for a visual builder made less sense as code, specifications and agents became our main working tools.
- [Test the flow before the next release: web prototypes and AI agents](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk-web-prototypes/): An idea is easier to discuss when you can walk through it. At EmTalk, I organise bounded web increments: I define behaviour and limits, then connect agent work through SDD, OpenSpec and checks of the built result.
- [EmTalk: a product ecosystem](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/emtalk/): Four connected directions: finding calm, understanding yourself, making decisions and developing skills. My contribution covers research, strategy, requirements and team coordination.
- [Kickidler: finding the causes of delay instead of asking for more speed](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/kickidler-delivery-system/): How I connected technical constraints, requirements and communication in one diagnosis, then developed a change plan.
- [Kickidler: supporting the people expected to change](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/kickidler-team-development/): A new process needs more than rules. How I worked on analysis practices, team development and feedback.
- [Kickidler: finding what was holding the product back](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/kickidler/): When delivery times, quality and team collaboration are connected, adding a process is not enough. I investigated the causes and prepared a change plan for a B2B product.
- [NeuroCity: proposing a shared product core for client projects](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/neurocity-product-core/): Client projects were being built from scratch, and deadlines were slipping. As Head of the Project Management Office, I prepared a proposal to develop a shared core and build client solutions around it.
- [Building a product on a tight budget: choosing channels, analytics and tools](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/product-without-budget/): My approach to choosing tools and channels while working on EmTalk: account for team time, maintenance and potential costs as usage grows.
- [No product analyst yet: building the tool myself](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/samolet-analytics/): Product decisions needed data. We did not yet have an analyst, and building dashboards through the usual process was difficult.
- [A CRM people rarely used: where I started changing things](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/samolet-delivery/): Sales agents and team leads preferred other tools. I began by researching their work and prioritising workflow fixes; the team and I then changed requirements and delivery.
- [A new sales approach: testing its value before scaling](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/samolet-sales-pilot/): Even a useful flow needs people to adopt it. For the same panel concept, we proposed starting with newcomers and deciding in advance how to compare meeting outcomes.
- [From presenting a housing development to discussing the customer's life](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/samolet-sales-story/): A sales manager needs to know the product; a buyer needs to understand how life could change. Our joint panel concept connects these needs through a meeting flow that adapts to the buyer's answers.
- [Statcontrol: testing the economics of change before implementation](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/statcontrol-economics-risks/): An organisational idea also needs a case for cost, payback and risk. How I turned a proposal into a financial model.
- [Statcontrol: when decisions depend on indispensable leaders](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/statcontrol-founder-bottleneck/): How I examined dependence on the founder and key managers, then designed an organisation that could distribute responsibility.
- [From industrial automation to digital twins](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/statcontrol/): From Honeywell DCS and OptiRamp digital twins to designing organisational change supported by financial and risk analysis.
- [WinLab's assortment matrix: from difficult discussions to requirements](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/winlab-assortment/): The retail chain wanted to expand regional assortments through local producers. Bringing other stakeholders into the discussion helped move the work forward.
- [Securing priority for a checkout project: a contractor conversation](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/winlab-checkout/): A move from a monolith to microservices and Kafka depended on the contractor. My task was to secure project priority and work towards meeting deadlines.
- [Automating 1C reporting: navigating difficult stakeholder discussions](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cases/winlab-reporting/): The challenge lay in stakeholder relationships. At one project meeting, the accounting team ended the discussion and left.
- [CV](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/cv/): Evgenii Zaitsev's experience, skills and education as a Product Manager across B2B and B2C. Download a short or full PDF CV.
- [EmTalk - the project and founder stories](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/emtalk/): The EmTalk story: team culture, Astana Hub, the move from a super app to an ecosystem and rethinking Tapl.
- [Privacy](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/privacy/): How visit statistics are collected on this site.
- [Questions and answers](https://evgenii42.github.io/en/questions/): Motivation, decisions, teams and working with AI. Each answer links to examples from my experience.

The full pages contain the context, attribution and limitations of individual results.
